# runpod_cluster (Resource)

A multi-node cluster of identical pods on one private overlay network. Only the name can be changed after creation: the compute shape, cluster type, and container configuration are fixed, so changing any of them replaces the cluster. Member pods are managed through the cluster, not through runpod_pod; read them with the runpod_cluster_pods data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "runpod_cluster" "training" {
  name              = "llama-finetune"
  type              = "TRAINING"
  gpu_type_id       = "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3"
  gpu_count_per_pod = 8
  pod_count         = 4
  image             = "runpod/pytorch:2.8.0-py3.11-cuda12.8.1-cudnn-devel-ubuntu22.04"
  disk              = 100
  ports             = ["22/tcp"]
  start_ssh         = true

  env = {
    NCCL_DEBUG = "INFO"
  }

  # A network volume shared by every member pod, in the same data center as the
  # cluster. Use mounts.persistent instead for host-local scratch space.
  mounts = {
    network = [{
      volume_id = runpod_network_volume.datasets.id
      path      = "/runpod-volume"
    }]
  }
}

output "cluster_entry_point" {
  description = "SSH into the primary node to drive the cluster."
  value       = runpod_cluster.training.primary_ssh_endpoint
}
```

Complete, runnable configurations that use this resource live in the use-case
modules under `v2/modules/` in the provider repository; the Guides section
documents each one.

## Schema

### Required

- `gpu_count_per_pod` (Number) Number of GPUs on each pod, bounded by the GPU type's per-cloud maximum. Total GPUs are pod_count * gpu_count_per_pod. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `gpu_type_id` (String) GPU type for every pod in the cluster, e.g. "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3". Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `name` (String) Cluster display name. The only attribute the API can change in place.
- `pod_count` (Number) Number of pods (nodes) in the cluster. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `type` (String) Cluster type: TRAINING for generic distributed training, SLURM for a managed Slurm controller/compute topology, RAY for a managed Ray head/worker topology, APPLICATION for a general multi-node application. Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Optional

- `args` (String) Arguments passed to the container entrypoint. Changing them replaces the cluster.
- `data_center_ids` (List of String) Preferred data centers for placement. Omit to let the scheduler choose; a cluster is always placed within a single data center, reported in data_center_id. Changing the preference replaces the cluster.
- `disk` (Number) Container disk in GB on each pod (ephemeral, wiped on restart). Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `env` (Map of String) Environment variables set on every member pod. Changing them replaces the cluster.
- `image` (String) Docker image every member pod runs. Public images only, because the cluster create input takes no registry credential. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `mounts` (Attributes) Storage mounted into every member pod. Set at most one of persistent and network. Changing a mount replaces the cluster. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mounts))
- `ports` (List of String) Exposed ports on every member pod, e.g. ["8888/http", "22/tcp"]. Changing them replaces the cluster.
- `start_jupyter` (Boolean) Start Jupyter on every member pod. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `start_ssh` (Boolean) Provision SSH access on every member pod by injecting the account's registered SSH public keys (see runpod_account_ssh_keys). Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp in RFC 3339 format.
- `data_center_id` (String) Data center the cluster was placed in, derived from the member pods. Null until at least one pod is placed.
- `id` (String) Cluster identifier assigned by the API.
- `network_cidr` (String) CIDR block of the cluster's private overlay network.
- `network_vxlan_id` (Number) VXLAN network identifier; null until assigned.
- `network_vxlan_port` (Number) UDP port carrying the VXLAN traffic; null until assigned.
- `pods_by_status` (Map of Number) Member pod counts keyed by pod status, e.g. {RUNNING = 4}. Statuses with no pods are absent.
- `pods_total` (Number) Number of member pods currently provisioned for the cluster.
- `primary_pod_id` (String) Pod id of the primary (rank 0) node: the Slurm controller or Ray head. Null until a primary pod is placed.
- `primary_ssh_endpoint` (String) Public SSH endpoint (host:port) of the primary node. Null until it is RUNNING with 22/tcp exposed.
- `primary_status` (String) Lifecycle status of the primary node, e.g. RUNNING, PROVISIONING.
- `template` (String) Template the member pods were created from; null when they were not created from one.

<a id="nestedatt--mounts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mounts`

Optional:

- `network` (Attributes List) An existing network volume mounted into every member pod. The API takes a list for forward compatibility but accepts at most one entry. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mounts--network))
- `persistent` (Attributes) Host-local persistent storage, pinned to each pod's host machine, so the data does not survive a host failure. Prefer a network mount for anything you cannot recreate. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mounts--persistent))

<a id="nestedatt--mounts--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mounts.network`

Required:

- `path` (String) Mount path inside the container, e.g. "/runpod-volume".
- `volume_id` (String) ID of a runpod_network_volume in the same data center as the cluster.


<a id="nestedatt--mounts--persistent"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mounts.persistent`

Required:

- `path` (String) Mount path inside the container, e.g. "/workspace".
- `size` (Number) Host-local storage in GB; the API enforces a 10 GB floor.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Clusters are imported by cluster id. The cluster object the API returns does
# not carry the container configuration, so an import leaves image, args, disk,
# env, ports, data_center_ids, mounts, start_ssh and start_jupyter empty in
# state. Each of them forces replacement: any one the configuration sets plans
# a new cluster on the first apply, even when it matches what the cluster was
# created with. Leave them out of the configuration, or name every one it sets
# in lifecycle { ignore_changes = [...] }, before the first apply.
terraform import runpod_cluster.training cluster_abc123
```
